context_for_next_agent: The load-bearing finding of this session is that STATUS_TRANSITIONS in frontend/lib/constants/request-status.ts is NOT the whole workflow rule, and the 2026-08-02 review assumed it was. It governs the single status-driven CTA button; the kebab menu separately offers supervisors two moves that deliberately leave the map — 'บังคับเสร็จสิ้น' (-> COMPLETED from any state) and 'ย้อนกลับ รอรับเรื่อง' (-> PENDING from any active state), both at page.tsx:659-660, both gated on can_assign. Enforcing the map as written would have 422'd six real transitions and broken working features. The owner chose to keep the menus and record the skips, so the rule now is: on-map = anyone; off-map + can_assign = allowed and logged as action='status_change_forced' with details.forced=true; off-map without can_assign = 422. If you ever add a new supervisor shortcut to the UI, it needs NO backend change — it will just be recorded as forced. If you instead widen STATUS_TRANSITIONS, you silently lose that distinction, which is why tests/test_request_workflow.py pins the six override moves as off-map. That same test file parses the .ts source and asserts the two maps are byte-identical, so editing one side alone now fails CI. HIGH-3 had FOUR call sites, not the two the review named: the fourth is the operator-initiated conversation endpoint (admin_live_chat.py, the POST that creates an ACTIVE session with an optional initial_message), whose broadcast was not wrapped at all. It needs db.refresh() between commit and fan-out, so it calls announce_session_event() while the other three use publish_session_event(). The invariant both enforce: once commit() returns, nothing may turn the operation back into an error; a commit failure still propagates because nothing is durable then. LOCAL RUNNER GOTCHA (new, not in the previous handoff): the full pytest run hangs near 99% on this Windows box — 872 tests collected, and it dies after ~10min with test_websocket.py pending. Run in-isolation it takes 50s and passes. Almost certainly leaked Redis connections or event loops accumulating over the preceding ~860 tests; CI splits jobs so it never sees this. Workaround that gives a real full-suite result: pytest --ignore=tests/test_websocket.py --ignore=tests/test_websocket_manager_redis.py --ignore=tests/test_ws_security.py (816 passed, ~3min), then run those three separately (46 + 10). Do NOT read a hang as a failure. Postgres+Redis were up for this session (docker compose up -d db redis) after Docker Desktop needed a hard restart — kill Docker Desktop + com.docker.backend, wsl --shutdown, relaunch; the backend had been waiting 31min on a dead engine while WSL distro docker-desktop sat Stopped. It cannot be done by an agent: cookie auth is SameSite=Strict so curl gets 401.
